name: Unikraft Cloud

modes.label: Self-serve plan pool (Hobby / Team / Pro concurrent running capacity)
modes.commit_note: Flat monthly plan; pool = concurrent RUNNING capacity. Scaled-to-zero (standby) instances do not consume it (Hobby 5 / Team 50 / Pro 5,000 standby). Pool month equals the plan fee (plans carry fee_is_credit=true so the fee is not charged twice).
modes.note: No metered rate or overage published; exceeding the running pool is presumably blocked by quota (unverified). Per-instance max RAM 8 GiB taken from the quotas-doc example account (not a published plan limit). A 4 vCPU / 8 GiB instance fits 1x on Team and 4x on Pro (memory-bound), none on Hobby.

modes.label: Enterprise: dedicated hosts / on-prem / BYOC (custom price)
modes.note: Unlimited instances, dedicated host fleet, on-prem/BYOC, named SRE, 1 h SLA. Enterprise-only: GPU preview (1 NVIDIA GPU/instance, QEMU 'full' VMs), arm64 hosts, nested virtualization, network shield (egress filtering + secret injection), sandbox plugin (exec/filesystem API). Customer story cites ~$0.30/h per browser at bare-metal economics (customer-reported, not a list price).

plans.name: Hobby
plans.note: Free forever, no card. 2 running instances (2 vCPU / 4 GiB total), 5 standby (8 GiB standby storage), 10 GiB image storage.

plans.name: Team
plans.note: $39/mo buys the Team pool (8 running instances, 8 vCPU / 8 GiB total), 50 standby (15 GiB), 50 GiB images, transparent migration. fee_is_credit=true only to avoid double-counting the identical pool tier price.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: $199/mo buys the Pro pool (24 running instances, 24 vCPU / 32 GiB total), 5,000 standby (1 TiB standby storage), 100 GiB images, user-defined proxy, snapshot history & rollback, live kernel updates, priority support.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom pricing; unlimited instances; dedicated hosts, on-prem/BYOC; SOC2/HIPAA/audit logs; 1 h SLA.

caveats: Unikraft Cloud publishes NO per-hour, per-GiB or egress price: self-serve pricing is a flat plan fee that caps concurrent running capacity (Hobby 2 vCPU/4 GiB/2 instances, Team 8 vCPU/8 GiB/8, Pro 24 vCPU/32 GiB/24). Anything bigger is Enterprise (custom price). Modelled as a pool mode.

Idle cost is $0 by design: scale-to-zero puts instances in standby in ~ms (stateful mode snapshots memory to disk) and standby instances don't count toward the running pool; standby storage included (8 GiB / 15 GiB / 1 TiB).

Self-serve sandbox ergonomics are limited: the sandbox plugin (command exec + filesystem API used by the JS SDK Sandbox class), network shield egress filtering, GPUs, arm64 and nested virtualization are Enterprise-only; instance forking is preview. Self-serve users deploy Dockerfile images as HTTP/TLS services.
Per-instance max vCPU/RAM per plan unpublished; max_ram_gib 8 comes from the quotas doc example (1 vCPU max there). The pool tiers may therefore overstate what a single instance can get.
Whether running above plan capacity is blocked or billed is not documented (no overage prices).
Egress/bandwidth not priced or capped on the pricing page; network values null.
snapshot_gib_month 0 = standby storage included within plan quota; no price for going beyond the quota.
Claimed <10 ms cold start / scale-to-zero is a vendor figure; no independent benchmark (perf null).
Regions: dal, fra, sfo, sin, was metros; 28 more listed as potential on request.
open_source=false for the platform; CLI/kraftkit/Terraform provider are open source (and the separate unikraft.org unikernel project).
Launched 2024-04-02 as KraftCloud (Launch HN, closed beta); rebranded Unikraft Cloud; domain now unikraft.com.

Re-checked 2026-09-28 (unikraft.com/pricing rendered in headless Chrome, unikraft.com/llms-full.txt): still no pay-as-you-go / per-instance / per-vCPU-hour rate; self-serve is only Hobby $0 / Team $39 / Pro $199 flat plans plus Enterprise custom. No PAYG regime can be carded.

fleet.tiers: Hobby 2 live/2 vCPU/4 GiB; Team 8 live/8 vCPU/8 GiB; Pro 24 live/24 vCPU/32 GiB; Enterprise custom. Standby 5/50/5,000 separately.
fleet.notes: All resource-pool caps apply together. 10 lightweight running instances need Pro; 50/300/1,000 running need Enterprise, even though 5,000 standby fit Pro. At 4 vCPU/8 GiB Pro holds only 4 by RAM. No quota approval SLA.

snapshot_auto.quote: With stateful scale-to-zero Unikraft Cloud takes a [snapshot](/features/snapshots) of the instance state before putting it into standby.
snapshot_auto.note: Opt-in (--scale-to-zero policy=on,stateful=true). Triggered when the instance idles into standby (no TCP/HTTP traffic for the cooldown); memory included, restored lazily on wake by the next request/packet. An explicit stop does NOT snapshot (stopped instances unmount volumes). Scheduled checkpoints via cron-style scheduled operations also exist.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A **checkpoint** captures the full state of an instance—its memory and volume state—at any moment, so you can later start new instances that resume from exactly that state.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Memory + volumes; taken from a running instance (pauses only a few ms, CoW); new instances boot from it, reusable many times; checkpoint history/rollback. Also branching (clone a live instance) and instance templates. Snapshot history & rollback listed as a Pro-plan feature.

harness_api.quote: The sandbox plugin lets you run commands and manipulate the filesystem inside an instance, over the plugin endpoint
harness_api.note: Only a generic exec/filesystem sandbox plugin (Enterprise); no API to drive Claude Code/Codex/etc. found in docs.

ingress_rules.quote: To connect to an instance from the Internet, you need to create a service and attach the instance to it.
ingress_rules.note: Instances are private by default (private IP + <name>.internal FQDN); a service maps chosen external FQDN ports to internal ports (TLS mandatory). Tunnel command for private access. No IP allowlist / auth on public URLs documented; plugin endpoints are authenticated.

volume_attach.quote: A volume is a persistent storage device that keeps data across restarts and even redeployments.
volume_attach.note: Block (ext4) volumes created/attached/detached via API/CLI/SDK; attach to running instance applies on next scale-to-zero cycle.

volume_shared.quote: `rwx`       | Read-write many. The volume can be mounted in read-write mode by multiple instances simultaneously. This access mode is only supported for volumes with `virtiofs` filesystem.
volume_shared.note: Read-write many via virtiofs volumes (slower than block); rox = read-only many for block volumes. BYOC/on-prem can add custom filesystem drivers (e.g. S3 via JuiceFS); managed host-path volumes Enterprise.
